rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object in Moses’ right hand is his staff; when he threw it, it became a serpent.
rows.anchor: يعنى عصاه، ففعل، فإذا هى حية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Taltaqaf” means “swallow”; the serpent swallowed the ropes and staffs produced by the magicians.
rows.anchor: يقول: تلقم { ما صنعوا } من السحر حتى تلقمت الحبال والعصى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The magicians’ production was a magician’s trick, while what Moses did was not magic.
rows.anchor: إن الذى عملوا هو عمل ساحر، يعنى كبيرهم، وما صنع موسى فليس بسحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A magician cannot succeed wherever he may be.
rows.anchor: أينما كان الساحر فلا يفلح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God caused the magicians to fall face down in prostration when the serpent swallowed the ropes and staffs.
rows.anchor: فلما التقمت الحبال والعصى ألقاهم الله، عز وجل، على وجوههم سجدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There were seventy-three magicians, and their chief was named Shamʿūn.
rows.anchor: وكانوا ثلاثة وسبعين ساحرا أكبرهم اسمه شمعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We believe” means “we affirm”; they affirm the Lord of Aaron and Moses.
rows.anchor: يعنى صدقنا { برب هارون وموسى } [آية: 70]

words: قَالَ ءَامَنتُمْ لَهُۥ قَبْلَ أَنْ ءَاذَنَ لَكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh addresses the magicians: they affirmed Moses before Pharaoh ordered them to believe in him.
rows.anchor: يعنى صدقتم لموسى { قبل أن ءاذن لكم } يقول: قبل أن آمركم بالإيمان لموسى

rows.speaker: فرعون
rows.claim: Pharaoh accuses Moses of being the magicians’ leader in magic and of teaching them.
rows.anchor: فرعون: { آمنتم له } يعنى صدقتم لموسى { قبل أن ءاذن لكم } يقول: قبل أن آمركم بالإيمان لموسى { إنه لكبيركم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cutting them crosswise means cutting the right hand and left foot.
rows.anchor: يعنى اليد اليمنى والرجل اليسرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here “in the trunks of the palms” means upon them, as in the cited wording from 52:38.
rows.anchor: يعنى عليه { ولتعلمن أينآ أشد عذابا وأبقى } [آية: 71]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh says they will learn whether he or the Lord of Moses and Aaron gives the harsher punishment.
rows.anchor: أنا أو ورب موسى وهارون { وأبقى } وأدوم عذابا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “More lasting” means more enduring punishment.
rows.anchor: وأبقى } وأدوم عذابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron is the speaker, addressing Moses as his mother’s son.
rows.anchor: هارون لموسى عليهما السلام: { يبنؤم لا تأخذ بلحيتي ولا برأسي }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron explains that if he had objected, the Israelites would have split into factions and killed one another.
rows.anchor: فإنى لو أنكرت لصاروا حزبين يقتل بعضهم بعضا

words: إِنِّى خَشِيتُ أَن تَقُولَ فَرَّقْتَ بَيْنَ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron feared Moses would accuse him of dividing Israel and disregarding the instruction to succeed him and set things right (7:142).
rows.anchor: يقول: ولم تحفظ وصيتى فى الأعراف قوله سبحانه لهارون:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron was more beloved to the Israelites than Moses; out of love for Aaron, they named seventy thousand of their children after him.
rows.anchor: وكان هارون أحب بنى إسرائيل من موسى، صلى الله عليهما، ولقد سمت بنو إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “What is your affair?” means “What is your matter?”; Moses asks the Samaritan what prompted what he sees.
rows.anchor: قال فما خطبك } يعنى فما أمرك؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Samaritan says he recognized what others had not about Gabriel’s horse.
rows.anchor: يقول: بما لم يفطنوا به يقول: عرفت ما لم يعرفوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The handful came from beneath Gabriel’s horse, from its hoofprint.
rows.anchor: يعنى تحت فرس جبريل، عليه السلام،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Samaritan threw the handful into the fire on top of the jewelry.
rows.anchor: فنبذتها } فى النار على أثر الحلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “My soul made it seem good to me” means his soul adorned the act for him.
rows.anchor: يقول: هكذا زينت لى نفسى أن أفعل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ sentence applies throughout the Samaritan’s life, until he dies.
rows.anchor: إلى أن تموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “No contact” means that the Samaritan must not mix with people.
rows.anchor: يعنى لا تخالط الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Samaritan also has an appointment in the afterlife, the Day of Resurrection, which he cannot miss.
rows.anchor: يعنى يوم القيامة { لن تخلفه } يقول: لن تغيب عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “god” Moses tells him to look at is the calf he worshipped.
rows.anchor: يعنى العجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Samaritan had remained devoted to worshipping the calf.
rows.anchor: يقول: أقمت عليه عابدا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The calf would be burned with fire and a rasp.
rows.anchor: بالنار وبالمبرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We will scatter it in the sea” means they would cast it away there.
rows.anchor: يقول: لننبذنه فى اليم نبذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Your family” means your people, as in the statement about Abraham commanding his family in 19:55.
rows.anchor: وكان يأمر أهله بالصلاة والزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is to pray and persist in prayer.
rows.anchor: يعنى الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not ask people for provision; what He asks of them is worship, and He provides for them.
rows.anchor: مآ أريد منهم من رزق ومآ أريد أن يطعمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The outcome of God-consciousness is the Garden.
rows.anchor: يعني عاقبة التقوى دار الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that God seeks worship, not provision, is linked to 51:56–57, where creation is for worship and God asks no provision or food.
rows.anchor: وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون مآ أريد منهم من رزق ومآ أريد أن يطعمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed concerning the unbelievers of Mecca.
rows.anchor: نزلت فى كفار مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are heedless of the reckoning and turn away because they do not believe in the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: لا يؤمنون به يعنى بالحساب يوم القيامة

words: مَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّن ذِكْرٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A “reminder from their Lord” means a clarification from God, namely the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: يعنى من بيان من ربهم يعنى القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Newly communicated” describes Qur’an God sends to the Prophet; it does not mean the Qur’an is originated with God.
rows.anchor: يقول: الذى يحدث الله، عز وجل، إلى النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم من القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They listen to the Qur’an while distracted and at play.
rows.anchor: يعنى لاهين عن القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their hearts are heedless of the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: يعنى غافلة قلوبهم عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who whisper are Abu Jahl, al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, and ʿUqba ibn Abi Muʿayt.
rows.anchor: فهو أبو جهل، والوليد بن المغيرة، وعقبة بن أبى معيط

rows.speaker: أبو جهل والوليد بن المغيرة وعقبة بن أبى معيط
rows.claim: They say Muhammad is only a human like them, with no distinction that would justify following him.
rows.anchor: قالوا سرا فيما بينهم: { هل هذآ } يعنون محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو جهل والوليد بن المغيرة وعقبة بن أبى معيط
rows.claim: They call the Qur’an magic and say that they can see it is magic.
rows.anchor: { أفتأتون السحر } يعنى القرآن { وأنتم تبصرون } [آية: 3] أنه سحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every messenger was sent with the revelation that there is no god but God, so people should worship and affirm His oneness.
rows.anchor: يعنى فوحدون

rows.speaker: النضر بن الحارث
rows.claim: Meccan unbelievers, including al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, claimed that the angels were God’s daughters; Muqatil rejects this claim.
rows.anchor: أى كفار مكة، منهم النضر بن الحارث { اتخذ الرحمن ولدا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels are honored servants who worship God, not daughters of the Merciful; God honored them through worship.
rows.anchor: لعبادة ربهم، وليسوا ببنات الرحمن، ولكن الله أكرمهم بعبادته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels do not precede God in speech or command, and they never instructed Meccan unbelievers to worship them.
rows.anchor: يقول: الملائكة لم تأمر كفار مكة بعبادتهم إياها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels act only by God’s command; they fear, sanctify, and worship their Lord.
rows.anchor: يقول: لا تعمل الملائكة إلا بأمره، فأخبر الله عز وجل عن الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The true promise is the promise of resurrection, which will certainly occur.
rows.anchor: يعنى وعد البعث أنه حق كائن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Staring” means open; the unbelievers will not blink at the wonders they see, which they denied in this life.
rows.anchor: يعنى فاتحة { أبصار الذين كفروا } بالبعث لا يطرفون مما يرون

words: قَدْ كُنَّا فِى غَفْلَةٍۢ مِّنْ هَٰذَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On seeing the Day of Resurrection, the unbelievers admit they were heedless of it and wrong because messengers warned them but they denied it.
rows.anchor: أخبرنا بهذا اليوم فكذبنا به

words: إِنَّكُمْ وَمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The addressees are Meccan unbelievers, and “what you worship” refers to the idols; they and their worshippers will be cast into Hell.
rows.anchor: يعنى كفار مكة { وما تعبدون من دون الله حصب جهنم } يعنى رميا فى جهنم ترمون فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Fuel of Hell” means something thrown into Hell.
rows.anchor: يعنى رميا فى جهنم ترمون فيها

words: لَوْ كَانَ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ ءَالِهَةًۭ مَّا وَرَدُوهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “These” are the idols; if they were gods, they would not enter Hell but would prevent themselves from entering.
rows.anchor: الأوثان { آلهة ما وردوها } يعنى ما دخلوها، يعنى جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “All” refers to the idols and their worshippers, who remain in Hell.
rows.anchor: يعنى الأوثان ومن يعبدها { فيها } يعنى فى جهنم { خالدون } [آية: 99]

words: إِنَّكُمْ وَمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage concerns Banu Sahm: al-ʿAs ibn Waʾil, al-Harith and ʿAdi ibn Qays, and ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zibara ibn Qays.
rows.anchor: نزلت فى بنى سهم، منهم: العاص بن وائل، والحارث وعدى ابنى قيس، وعبد الله بن الزبعرى بن قيس

words: إِنَّكُمْ وَمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet pointed to the 360 idols around the Kaaba and recited these verses to Banu Sahm while they sat in the Hatim.
rows.anchor: أن النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم دخل المسجد الحرام، ونفر من بنى سهم جلوس فى الحطيم

words: إِنَّكُمْ وَمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبعرى
rows.claim: After hearing the recitation from Banu Sahm, Ibn al-Zibara said he would defeat the Prophet if he said it in his presence, then asked whether it applied only to their idols or to all peoples’ idols.
rows.anchor: فقال الزبعرى: والله، لئن قالها بين يدى لأخصمنه.

words: إِنَّكُمْ وَمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet answered that the warning applied to them, their idols, and all peoples and their idols.
rows.anchor: فقال النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم: " لكم ولآلهتكم ولجميع الأمم ولآلهتهم ".

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبعرى
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zibara argued that Jesus, Mary, ʿUzayr, and angels were worshipped and would therefore be included; the Prophet fell silent.
rows.anchor: قال: خصمتك ورب الكعبة، ألست تزعم أن عيسى نبى، وتثنى عليه، وعلى أمه خيرا

words: إِن كُنتُمْ فِى رَيْبٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْبَعْثِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqatil addresses the unbelievers of Mecca, who doubt resurrection, and urges them to consider how they were first created.
rows.anchor: يعنى كفار مكة { إن كنتم فى ريب من البعث } يعنى فى شك من البعث بعد الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings began as nothing and were created from earth.
rows.anchor: ولم تكونوا شيئا

words: ثُمَّ مِن نُّطْفَةٍۢ ثُمَّ مِنْ عَلَقَةٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clot (“ʿalaqa”) is like blood.
rows.anchor: مثل الدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The formed morsel is formed from the drop of fluid.
rows.anchor: يعنى من النطقة مخلقة { وغير مخلقة } يعنى السقط يخرج من بطن أمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unformed morsel is a miscarriage: it may leave the womb formed or unformed.
rows.anchor: يعنى السقط يخرج من بطن أمه مصورا، وغير مصور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God keeps in the womb what He wills, so it does not miscarry, until its appointed term and birth.
rows.anchor: فلا يكون سقطا { إلى أجل مسمى } يقول: خروجه من بطن أمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The age of full strength runs from eighteen to forty years.
rows.anchor: ثمانى عشرة سنة إلى أربعين سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some die before reaching full strength; others, after youth, return to the decrepit age of old age and lose what they once knew.
rows.anchor: من قبل أن يبلغ أشده { ومنكم من يرد } بعد الشباب { إلى أرذل العمر } يعنى الهرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is dead, without plants, and broken or crumbling.
rows.anchor: يعنى ميتة ليس فيها نبت يعنى متهشمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth “moves” with vegetation; 28:31 compares this movement to a serpent.
rows.anchor: الأرض، يعنى تحركت بالنبات، كقوله: تهتز كأنها جآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth increases and multiplies its vegetation.
rows.anchor: يعنى وأضعفت النبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It produces every beautiful kind of plant.
rows.anchor: يعنى من كل صنف من النبات حسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stages of human creation and the revival of dead earth demonstrate resurrection: the One who began creation can restore the dead.
rows.anchor: ليعتبروا فى البعث، فإن البعث ليس بأشد من بدء الخلق، ومن الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Have you not seen?” means “Have you not known?”
rows.anchor: يعنى ألم تعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those in the heavens who prostrate include angels and others.
rows.anchor: من الملائكة وغيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun, moon, and stars prostrate to God beneath the Throne when they set, before the evening prayer.
rows.anchor: سجود هؤلاء الثلاثة حين تغرب الشمس قبل المغرب لله تعالى تحت العرش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mountains, trees, and animals prostrate through their shadows at sunrise and when the sun passes its zenith, as each shadow shifts.
rows.anchor: ظلهم حين تطلع الشمس، وحين تزول إذا تحول ظل كل شىء فهو سجوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The many people who prostrate are believers; those who deserve punishment are unbelievers among humans and jinn, whose prostration is their shadows.
rows.anchor: من كفار الإنس والجن سجودهم هو سجود ظلالهم

words: وَمَن يُهِنِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن مُّكْرِمٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God determines what happens among His creation; one whom He humiliates has no one to honor.
rows.anchor: يفعل ما يشاء } [آية: 18] فى خلقه

words: أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَسْجُدُ لَهُۥ
rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When the Prophet recited this verse, he and his Companions prostrated.
rows.anchor: فقرأ النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم هذه الآية فسجد لها هو وأصحابه، رضى الله عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meccan unbelievers tortured some believers and verbally harmed others until they fled from Mecca to Medina.
rows.anchor: ذلك أنهم عذبوا منهم طائفة، وآذوا بعضهم بالألسن

words: بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ إِلَّآ أَن يَقُولُوا۟ رَبُّنَا ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers were expelled only for saying that God was their Lord, knowing and affirming His oneness.
rows.anchor: إلا أن يقولوا: { ربنا الله } فعرفوه ووحدوه

words: وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God did not repel polytheists through Muslims, the polytheists would overcome and kill the Muslims.
rows.anchor: لولا أن يدفع الله المشركين بالمسلمين لغلب المشركون فقتلوا المسلمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The protected worship places are monks’ hermitages, Christian churches, Jewish prayer houses, and Muslim mosques.
rows.anchor: { صوامع } الرهبان { وبيع } النصارى { وصلوات } يعنى اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These religious communities remember God frequently in their worship places, which Muslims protect by repelling the polytheists.
rows.anchor: كل هؤلاء الملل يذكرون الله كثيرا فى مساجدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will help whoever aids Him by affirming His oneness; He is strong in helping His allies and invincible in His dominion.
rows.anchor: يعن من يعينه حتى يوحد الله، عز وجل،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording “who helps Him” is linked to 57:25, where it means whoever affirms God’s oneness.
rows.anchor: يعني من يوحده، وغيرها فى الأحزاب، وهود.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is more protective and mightier than His creation.
rows.anchor: وهو سبحانه أوقى وأعز من خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For earlier peoples, a “manasak” means a sacrifice involving the shedding of sacrificial blood at their festival.
rows.anchor: يعنى لكل قوم فيما خلا { جعلنا منسكا } يعنى ذبحا، يعنى هراقة الدماء ذبيحة فى عيدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They perform it” means they slaughter the sacrifice; the same word “nusuk” means sacrifice in 6:162.
rows.anchor: يعني ذبيحتي { فلا ينازعنك في الأمر } يعنى فى أمر الذبائح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dispute concerns sacrifices; Muhammad is more entitled to the matter than the unbelievers of Khuzāʿa and others.
rows.anchor: يعنى فى أمر الذبائح، فإنك أولى بالأمر منهم، أي من كفار خزاعة وغيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about Badil ibn Warqa, Bishr ibn Sufyan al-Khuzaʿi, and Yazid ibn al-Halbas of Banu al-Harith ibn ʿAbd Manaf.
rows.anchor: نزلت فى بديل بن ورقاء الخزاعى، وبشر بن سفيان الخزاعي، ويزيد بن الحلبس، من بني الحارث بن عبد مناف

rows.speaker: بديل بن ورقاء وبشر بن سفيان ويزيد بن الحلبس
rows.claim: They told the Muslims that animals killed by their own hands were lawful but those killed by God—carrion—were forbidden.
rows.anchor: لقولهم للمسلمين، فى الأنعام، ما قتلتم أنتم بأيديكم فهو حلال وما قتل الله فهو حرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call is to know God through affirming His oneness; the Prophet follows the straight religion.
rows.anchor: يعني إلى معرفة ربك وهو التوحيد { إنك لعلى هدى } يعني لعلى دين { مستقيم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The human” created from clay is Adam.
rows.anchor: يعنى آدم صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Sullāla” is the material drawn out when clay is squeezed, with clay and water slipping between the fingers.
rows.anchor: والسلالة: إذا عصر الطين انسل الطين والماء من بين أصابعه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The drop of fluid is Adam’s progeny.
rows.anchor: يعنى ذرية آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The secure lodging is the womb, where the drop is established.
rows.anchor: يعنى الرحم: تمكن النطفة فى الرحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fluid changes into blood; the blood then changes into flesh like a morsel, followed by bones covered with flesh.
rows.anchor: يقول: تحول الماء فصار دما { فخلقنا العلقة مضغة } يعنى فتحول الدم فصار لحما مثل المضغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “other creation” is the spirit, breathed into the body after its physical creation.
rows.anchor: يقول: خلقناه، { خلقا آخر } يعنى الروح ينفخ فيه بعد خلقه

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Before the Prophet finished the verse, ʿUmar recited its closing words; the Prophet told him, “Thus it was revealed, ʿUmar.”
rows.anchor: فقال عمر بن الخطاب، رضى الله عنه: قبل أن يتم النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم الآية: { تبارك الله أحسن الخالقين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the best image-maker compared with those who make statues and other things that cannot move.
rows.anchor: يقول: هو أحسن المصورين، يعني من الذين خلقوا التماثيل وغيرها التى لا يتحرك منها شىء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the completion of human creation, people die at their appointed times.
rows.anchor: الخلق بعد ما ذكر من تمام خلق الإنسان { لميتون } [آية: 15] عند آجالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After death, people are brought back to life on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: يعنى تحيون بعد الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven paths are seven heavens; each is 500 years’ journey thick, with 500 years’ journey between each heaven.
rows.anchor: يعنى سموات غلظ كل سماء مسيرة خمس مائة عام، وبين كل سماء مسيرة خمس مائة عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is not heedless of creating the heavens or anything else.
rows.anchor: يعنى عن خلق السماء وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sends enough water for people’s livelihood, including springs.
rows.anchor: ما يكفيكم من المعيشة، يعنى العيون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We lodged it” means “We placed it” in the earth.
rows.anchor: يعنى فجعلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can make the water sink into the earth until it cannot be reached.
rows.anchor: فيغور فى الأرض، يعنى فلا يقدر عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Tastaʾnisū” means “ask permission.”
rows.anchor: يعني حتى تستأذنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order implies greeting first and asking permission afterward.
rows.anchor: فيها تقديم فابدءوا بالسلام قبل الاستئذان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before this verse, people greeted one another in pre-Islamic fashion with “Good morning and evening”; the verse institutes greeting and permission.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنهم كانوا فى الجاهلية يقول بعضهم لبعض: حييت صباحا ومساء، فهذه كانت تحية القوم بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Greeting and asking permission are better than entering without leave, and allow the household to be ready.
rows.anchor: يعنى السلام والاستئذان { خير لكم } يعنى أفضل لكم من أن تدخلوا بغير إذن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If no one is in the house, do not enter until permission is given; if told to return, leave rather than linger at the door because people have their own needs.
rows.anchor: ولا تقعدوا ولا تقوموا على أبواب الناس، فإن لهم حوائج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning when asked is better than standing or sitting at the door.
rows.anchor: هو أزكى لكم } يقول: الرجعة خير لكم من القيام والقعود على أبوابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows whether people enter with or without permission; the two recording angels rebuke an unauthorized entrant for disobeying God and harming the household.
rows.anchor: فمن دخل بيتا بغير إذن أهله، قال له ملكاه اللذان يكتبان عليه: أف لك

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
rows.claim: Abu Bakr asked the Prophet about roadside houses between Mecca, Medina, and Syria that had no residents; the verse was revealed in answer.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر الصديق، رضى الله عنه، للنبى صلى الله عليه وسلم: فكيف بالبيوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Uninhabited houses may be entered without blame; they include inns and hotels whose provisions shelter travelers from cold and heat.
rows.anchor: ليس بها ساكن { فيها متاع } يعنى منافع { لكم } من البرد والحر

words: وَٱللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا تُبْدُونَ وَمَا تَكْتُمُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what people disclose with their tongues and what they keep hidden in their hearts.
rows.anchor: { والله يعلم ما تبدون } يعنى ما تعلنون بألسنتكم { وما تكتمون } [آية: 29] يعنى ما تسرون فى قلوبكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mockery of the Prophet was revealed concerning Abu Jahl.
rows.anchor: نزلت فى أبى جهل لعنه الله

rows.speaker: أبو جهل
rows.claim: Abu Jahl mocks Muhammad by asking whether this is the man God sent as a messenger.
rows.anchor: أهذا الذى بعث الله رسولا

rows.speaker: أبو جهل
rows.claim: Abu Jahl says Muhammad nearly turned them away from worshipping their gods and into his religion.
rows.anchor: يعنى ليستزلنا عن عبادة آلهتنا، { لولا أن صبرنا } يعنى تثبتنا { عليها } يعنى على عبادتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When they see punishment, they will learn who strayed from guidance—them or the believers.
rows.anchor: يعنى من أخطأ طريق الهدى أهم أم المؤمنون

rows.speaker: الحارث بن قيس السهمى
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about al-Harith ibn Qays al-Sahmi, who desired something and worshipped it.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن الحارث بن قيس السهمى هوى شيئا فعبده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is not a controller over such a person; the Prophet wants to change the person’s choice between guidance and error.
rows.anchor: يعنى مسيطرا يقول: تريد أن تبدل المشيئة إلى الهدى والضلالة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A newly communicated reminder is Qur’an that God sends to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: يقول: ما يحدث الله عز وجل إلى النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم من القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They turn away from believing in the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: يعنى عن الإيمان بالقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They denied the truth, meaning the Qur’an, when it came with Muhammad.
rows.anchor: بالحق، يعنى بالقرآن لما جاءهم، يعنى حين جاءهم محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God threatened them with death at Badr because they had denied the Qur’an; the news of what they mocked would reach them.
rows.anchor: أوعدهم الله عز وجل بالقتل ببدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth produces many beautiful kinds and colors of plants.
rows.anchor: كم أخرجنا من الأرض من كل صنف من ألوان النبت حسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plants are a sign proving God’s oneness.
rows.anchor: إن فى النبت لعبرة فى توحيد الله عز وجل، أنه واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most of those who did not believe in God’s oneness were the people of Mecca.
rows.anchor: يعنى أهل مكة { مؤمنين } [آية: 8] يعنى مصدقين بالتوحيد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “When your Lord called” means when God commanded Moses; the address is to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: يقول: وإذ أمر ربك يا محمد { موسى أن ائت القوم الظالمين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oppressive people are polytheists.
rows.anchor: يعنى المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of Pharaoh were in Egypt, and Pharaoh’s name was Fitus.
rows.anchor: واسمه فيطوس بأرض مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Will they not be God-conscious?” means “Will they not worship God?”
rows.anchor: يعنى ألا يعبدون الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses fears that the people will call him a liar in what he says.
rows.anchor: فيما أقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ chest becoming constricted means his heart becoming constricted.
rows.anchor: يعنى يضيق قلبى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses fears his tongue will not be free to deliver the message.
rows.anchor: يعنى يضيق قلبى، { ولا ينطلق لسانى } بالبلاغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks for Aaron to be sent along with him; “to” here means “with,” as in 4:2.
rows.anchor: يقول: فأرسل معى هارون، كقوله فى النساء:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The offense Moses has against them is his killing of a person.
rows.anchor: يعنى عندى ذنب، يعنى قتل النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses fears Pharaoh’s people will kill him.
rows.anchor: فأخاف أن يقتلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tells Moses and Aaron not to fear being killed and commands both to go with His signs.
rows.anchor: لا تخافا القتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah’s people denied Noah alone; the same pattern appears in the account in Surat al-Qamar (54:9).
rows.anchor: يعنى كذبوا نوحا وحده، نظيرها فى اقتربت الساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah was their brother by lineage, not by religion.
rows.anchor: ليس بأخيهم فى الدين، ولكن أخوهم فى النسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call to be God-conscious means to fear God.
rows.anchor: يعنى ألا تخشون الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah is trustworthy in what lies between the people and their Lord.
rows.anchor: فيما بينكم وبين ربكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Fear God” means worship God; obey Noah in the counsel he gives.
rows.anchor: يعنى فاعبدوا الله { وأطيعون } [آية: 108] فيما آمركم به من النصيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah asks no payment for calling people to faith; the prophets answer an accusation that they seek control of people’s wealth.
rows.anchor: يعنى جعلا، وذلك أنهم قالوا للأنبياء: إنما تريدون أن تملكوا علينا فى أموالنا

words: إِنْ أَجْرِىَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ ٱلْعَٰلَمِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “My reward” means “my recompense,” which comes only from the Lord of the worlds.
rows.anchor: يعنى جزائى { إلا على رب العالمين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah repeats that the people should follow his counsel.
rows.anchor: فيما آمركم به من النصيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “lowly” followers are the rabble or common people.
rows.anchor: يعنى السفلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah says he could not know that God would guide those people to faith while leaving the others.
rows.anchor: لم أكن أعلم أن الله يهدىهم للإيمان من بينكم ويدعكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reckoning and recompense of the people whom Noah’s opponents call lowly belongs to God.
rows.anchor: يعنى ما جزاء الأرذلون { إلا على ربى لو تشعرون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “If you were aware” means if you understood.
rows.anchor: لو تشعرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah will not refuse believers whom his opponents regard as lowly.
rows.anchor: وما أنا بالذى لا يقبل الإيمان من الذين تزعمون أنهم الأرذلون عندكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah says he is only a clear messenger and warner.
rows.anchor: { إلا نذير مبين } [آية: 115] يعنى رسول بين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “If you do not desist” means “if you do not stop speaking to us.”
rows.anchor: يعنى لئن لم تسكت { ينوح } عنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat to stone Noah means they would kill him.
rows.anchor: يعنى من المقتولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah says his people denied the resurrection.
rows.anchor: نوح: { رب إن قومى كذبون } [آية: 117] البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah asks God to judge between them; the judgment means punishment.
rows.anchor: يقول: اقض بينى وبينهم قضاء، يعنى العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah asks to be saved from drowning with the believers, and God saved him.
rows.anchor: من الغرق، فنجاه الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud was their brother by lineage, not by religion.
rows.anchor: ليس بأخيهم فى الدين ولكن أخوهم فى النسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Will you not be God-conscious?” means “Will you not fear God?”
rows.anchor: يعنى ألا تخشون الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud is trustworthy in what lies between the people and their Lord.
rows.anchor: فيما بينكم وبين ربكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Fear God” means worship God; Hud calls them to obey his counsel.
rows.anchor: يعنى فاعبدوا الله، { وأطيعون } [آية: 126] فيما آمركم به من النصيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud asks no payment for faith; his reward is only from the Lord of the worlds.
rows.anchor: يقول: لا أسألكم على الإيمان جعلا { إن أجرى } يقول: ما أجرى { إلا على رب العالمين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A “rīʿ” is a road, and an “āya” here is a marker or landmark.
rows.anchor: يعنى طريق { آية } يعنى علما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people built useless tall palaces as road markers; they otherwise navigated by the stars.
rows.anchor: يعنى تلعبون، وذلك أنهم كانوا إذا سافروا لا يهتدون إلا بالنجوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Maṣāniʿ” are palaces, used to identify whose lodging a place was.
rows.anchor: يعنى القصور ليذكروا بها هذا منزل بنى فلان، وبنى فلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They acted as though they would remain forever in this world and never die.
rows.anchor: فى الدنيا فلا تموتون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamud denied Ṣalih alone.
rows.anchor: يعنى صالحا وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣalih was their brother by lineage.
rows.anchor: فى النسب، وليس بأخيهم فى الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Will you not be God-conscious?” means “Will you not fear God?”
rows.anchor: يعنى ألا تخشون الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣalih is trustworthy in what lies between the people and God.
rows.anchor: فيما بينكم وبين الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣalih urges them to worship God and obey his instructions.
rows.anchor: فيما آمركم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣalih asks no payment for faith; his recompense comes only from the Lord of the worlds.
rows.anchor: يعنى على الإيمان { من أجر } يعنى جعلا { إن أجرى } يعنى جزائى { إلا على رب العالمين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣalih asks whether they think they will safely keep enjoying the good things they have, without dying.
rows.anchor: من الخير { آمنين } [آية: 146] من الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good things include gardens, springs, crops, and date palms.
rows.anchor: { فى جنات وعيون } [آية: 147] { وزروع ونخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The date palm’s spadix is “dense”: its parts are layered together in abundance.
rows.anchor: يعنى طلعها متراكب بعضها على بعض من الكثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They carved mountain homes skillfully; “fārihīn” means proficient.
rows.anchor: يعنى حاذقين بنحتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣalih again urges them to worship God and follow his counsel.
rows.anchor: فيما آمركم به من النصيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “transgressors” are the nine men who hamstrung the she-camel.
rows.anchor: يعنى التسعة الذين عقروا الناقة

words: ٱلَّذِينَ يُفْسِدُونَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَلَا يُصْلِحُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cause corruption by disobeying God and do not obey what He commands.
rows.anchor: يقول: الذين يعصون فى الأرض، ولا يطيعون الله عز وجل، فيما أمرهم به

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة والفراء
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayda and al-Farraʾ say “musahhar” means a created being.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة والفراء: المسحر المخلوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes “musahhar” as someone with a saḥr where food gathers beneath the throat; the neck’s upper half is called naḥr and lower half saḥr.
rows.anchor: ويقال أيضا: الذى له سحر يجتمع فيه طعامه أسفل نحره، لأن نصف العنق نحر، ونصفه سحر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot’s people denied Lot alone.
rows.anchor: كذبوا لوطا وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot was Lūṭ ibn Ḥarāz ibn Āzar, and Sarah was Lot’s sister.
rows.anchor: ولوط بن حراز بن آزر، فسارة أخت لوط، عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Will you not be God-conscious?” means “Will you not fear God?”
rows.anchor: يعنى ألا تخشون الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot declares that he is a trustworthy messenger.
rows.anchor: إني لكم رسول أمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot calls them to worship God and follow his counsel.
rows.anchor: فيما آمركم به من النصيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot asks for no payment for their faith; his reward is from the Lord of the worlds.
rows.anchor: يعنى ما أسألكم على الإيمان من جعل { إن أجرى } يعنى ما جزائى { إلا على رب العالمين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Approaching the males” means having sex with men.
rows.anchor: يعنى نكاح الرجال

words: وَتَذَرُونَ مَا خَلَقَ لَكُم مِّنْ أَزْوَٰجِكُم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God created for them in their wives means the women’s sexual organs.
rows.anchor: يعنى بالأزواج فروج نسائكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are a transgressing people.
rows.anchor: يعنى معتدين

rows.speaker: قوم لوط
rows.claim: Lot’s people threaten to expel him from the town unless he stops speaking against them.
rows.anchor: يعنى لئن لم تسكت عنا { يلوط لتكونن من المخرجين } [آية: 167] من القرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot says he detests their practice of sex with men; he glosses “al-qālīn” as “al-muqātīn.”
rows.anchor: يعنى إتيان الرجال { من القالين } [آية: 168] يعنى المقاتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot asks to be saved with his family from their filthy acts.
rows.anchor: من الخبائث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God saved Lot and all his family.
rows.anchor: فنجيناه وأهله أجمعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The old woman left among those punished was Lot’s wife.
rows.anchor: يعنى الباقين فى العذاب يعنى امرأته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God destroyed the others by subsidence and stones.
rows.anchor: يعنى أهلكنا { الآخرين } [آية: 172] بالخسف والحصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rain was stones; God caused Lot’s towns to collapse and sent stones against those outside the town.
rows.anchor: يعنى الحجارة { فسآء } يعنى فبئس { مطر المنذرين } [آية: 173] يعنى الذين أنذروا بالعذاب
